findings.finding: A verdict's binding to 'this claim' is only as unique as (transcriptId, item, claim opId), and nothing makes transcript ids unique. The scope's tenantId, profileDigest, bundleDigest, routeId and routeDigest are unconstrained, and the topology is not part of the scope. Probe P02: a ledger written for transcript id 'probe-1' under tenant 'tenant-zz' binds in another run that reuses the id 'probe-1' (same item i1, same claim opId a1), and the holder's MERGE is ACCEPTED. So the round-1 disposition's claim that one ledger cannot verify another claim holds within one transcript, but not across board runs or tenants that reuse ids. No vector covers it: a mutant that compares only the item part of subjectId (N15) passes every vector.
findings.requiredChange: Make the claim's name unique: for example, bind the topology digest into the scope (routeDigest = topologyDigest, or include it in subjectId), and state that a transcript id is unique per board run and tenant. Otherwise list the assumption under Not claimed. Add a vector: a ledger for the same transcript/item/claim names but another run (another tenant or topology) is LEDGER_MISMATCH.

findings.location: scripts/topology_coordination.py _Board._verify (check_history over the claim's ledgers); README A2 'Verdict history'
findings.finding: The history rule allows one work per claim, and the README does not say so. A MAS-RA-001 history keeps one subject, and the scope's subjectDigest (the work) is part of that subject. So once a claim has a verdict, a verdict on revised work is VERDICT_HISTORY, whether the new ledger is fresh or supersedes the old one. Probes P01a and P01b: FAIL on work A, then PASS on revised work B, gives VERDICT_HISTORY and then VERDICT_NOT_PASS on the merge of B. Revision works only by RELEASE and a new claim (P01c), which in decentralized mode opens the item to other workers. The README's 'a superseding ledger may make the status better (on new evidence)' reads as if a fix-and-reverify loop works within a claim; it works only for the same work.
findings.requiredChange: Either state it ('one work per claim: a revised delivery needs a new claim') and add a vector, or keep a history per (claim, work digest), as MAS-RA-001 treats a revised delivery as a new subject, with MERGE reading the latest verdict on the merged work.
